summary: The archived v3 orchestration falsely rejects an unchanged protected source inventory: line-delimited ls-tree C-quotes five Greek/ß filenames, while ls-files -z returns literal paths. Both NUL-delimited sets have 3582 identical members. This focused observation preserves the real #1126 finding against immutable v3 evidence; it does not claim v4 remains defective or grant final-head approval.

assessments.summary: The exact membership guard itself is appropriate. Its baseline side uses line-delimited Git output that C-quotes non-ASCII filenames; the current side uses literal NUL-delimited output. Five names differ only in representation. Independent NUL comparison proves both protected sets have the same 3582 members.

findings.title: Post1122 preflight compares quoted Git paths with literal Unicode paths
findings.description: The v3 baseline ls-tree --name-only output is line-delimited and C-quotes five non-ASCII filenames. Current ls-files -z output is literal. Exact set equality falsely fails although independent ls-tree -z and ls-files -z inventories both contain the same 3582 protected source paths. A versioned NUL-parser correction can preserve the exact membership guard.
